newsitem.title: POLAND: Unknown Handlowy IPO inflows seen boosting zloty.
newsitem.headline: Unknown Handlowy IPO inflows seen boosting zloty.

text.p: The zloty was bullish again on Tuesday as potential capital inflows into Bank Handlowy SA's one billion zloty IPO created strong currency selling pressure.
But most of the market remains in the dark about the extent and timing of foriegn entry into Handlowy shares.
"There is a large amount of currencies on the market but it is not clear where it's coming from. Eveyone is looking at the Handlowy IPO but nobody is certain," said one dealer in Warsaw.
Dealers said Germany's Commerzbank AG further entry into Bank Rozwoju Eksportu SA (BRE) shares, cleared by the securites commision last week, also created upward pressure on the zloty.

The zloty closed at 1.52/1.50 percent from the trading band centre, flat from Monday's close at 1.53/1.49 percent after the National Bank of Poland (NBP) bought some $30-$50 million through interventions on Tuesday, dealers said.
It closed at 3.2440/46 to the dollar, down from 3.2390/00 on Monday and at 1.8693/98 to the mark, up from 1.8703/13.
The central bank bought dollars at 3.2450 zlotys, or when the zloty was about 1.52 percent from parity.
"The NBP will have problems in keeping the zloty at 1.5 percent from parity without intervening everyday," said Witold Wozniak, forex dealer at Deutsche Bank Poska SA.

The finance ministry announced earlier on Tuesday that Poland will issue its first U.S. SEC-registered bonds in coming weeks, with JP Morgan leading the issue along with co-managers Merrill Lynch & Co. and Salomon Brothers Inc..
The ministry did not give the amount of the issue, but under budget law Poland cannot issue more than $500 million worth of bonds on international markets in 1997.

The government will lower its official inflation target to year-on-year 12 percent in December this year from the current 13 percent plan, after price growth was smaller then expected in the first five months of 1997, the finance minister said.
